1.title: From Pomace to Precious Spirit
1.html:
Marc d'Alsace Gewurztraminer is a distinctive Alsace spirit, confirmed by decree in 1966 as a regulated appellation of origin, and today a protected designation of origin (AOP).

The raw material rules are extremely strict: it must use Gewurztraminer pomace (marc) harvested within the AOP Alsace area, and distillation must be completed within the two départements of Haut-Rhin and Bas-Rhin. The pomace must be healthy and fully destemmed, and every 100 kg of declared raw material must be able to yield at least 4.5 litres of pure alcohol.
2.title: Rigorous Distillation Rules
2.html:
• Distillation method: two-stage distillation in a traditional pot still (alambic à repasse) — the use of rectification columns (colonnes de rectification) is expressly forbidden, to preserve the rustic, intense aroma character of the pomace itself
  • Strength at distillation: must be below 68° GL as it leaves the still
  • Strength at sale: must be at least 45° GL when bottled for sale
  • Non-alcohol substance content: at least 300 g per hundred litres of pure alcohol (300 g/hl pure alcohol; these substances are exactly what gives Marc its intense aroma and personality)

💡 Because the raw material is exactly the Gewurztraminer skins and seeds (the solids left after pressing), Marc d'Alsace Gewurztraminer can often concentrate the variety's most exuberant rose, lychee and spice character — a highly representative spirit in Alsace's after-dinner culture.
3.question: What does the Marc d'Alsace Gewurztraminer regulation expressly forbid in distillation?
3.options.0: The use of the traditional pot still is forbidden
3.options.1: The use of rectification columns (colonnes de rectification) is forbidden, to preserve the pomace's own intense aroma character
3.explanation: The Marc d'Alsace Gewurztraminer regulation expressly forbids the use of rectification columns (colonnes de rectification), allowing only two-stage distillation in a traditional pot still (alambic à repasse) — a rule meant to preserve the rustic, intense aroma character of the pomace itself and avoid a rectification column purifying it so far that it loses its personality.
4.keyPoints.0: Confirmed in 1966 as a regulated appellation of origin (now AOP), raw material limited to Gewurztraminer pomace from the AOP Alsace area
4.keyPoints.1: Every 100 kg of raw material must be able to yield at least 4.5 litres of pure alcohol
4.keyPoints.2: Two-stage distillation in a traditional pot still, with rectification columns expressly forbidden
4.keyPoints.3: Below 68° GL at distillation and at least 45° GL at sale, with non-alcohol substances of at least 300 g/hl pure alcohol
